questions.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 & 14 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ -52 & 0 & -12 & -32 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

I. ${R}_{1}:=…$

II. ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}$

III. ${R}_{3}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{4},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
questions.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above ${a}_{42}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 & 14 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ -52 & 0 & -12 & -32 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{4}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{4}.$
